title: Experimental Realization Of Qubit-state-controlled Directional Edge States In Waveguide Qed
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 03 June 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration of qubit-state-controlled directional edge states in a waveguide QED system, enabling on-chip routing of quantum information.
motivation: To realize controllable directional emission and routing of photons in waveguide QED, which is crucial for quantum networks and on-chip quantum information processing.
method: Using superconducting qubits coupled to a waveguide with engineered chiral coupling, the authors demonstrate that the qubit state controls the direction of edge state propagation.
result: They achieve high-fidelity directional control of edge states, with the propagation direction determined by the qubit state, showing potential for quantum routing.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable approach to quantum routing in waveguide QED, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking applications.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of A Two-voter Quantum Anonymous Voting Prototype With Continuous Variables
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a two-voter quantum anonymous voting protocol using continuous-variable quantum states.
motivation: Anonymous voting is a key multi-party cryptographic task; quantum protocols can provide information-theoretic security. This work aims to realize such a protocol experimentally.
method: The authors implement a two-voter quantum anonymous voting scheme using continuous-variable quantum states (likely coherent states) and homodyne detection, demonstrating the core steps of ballot casting and tallying.
result: Successful experimental demonstration of quantum anonymous voting with two voters, showing feasibility of the protocol with current technology.
conclusion: The experiment validates the practical viability of continuous-variable quantum anonymous voting, paving the way for larger-scale quantum network applications.

title: Lieb–Liniger Interaction Via Self-interacting Stationary Light Polaritons
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes a scheme to realize the Lieb-Liniger model using self-interacting stationary light polaritons in a cold atomic ensemble.
motivation: To simulate strongly correlated quantum many-body systems, specifically the Lieb-Liniger model of bosons with contact interactions, using a photonic platform that allows for tunable interactions.
method: The authors use electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to create stationary light polaritons, and introduce a Kerr nonlinearity to mediate effective interactions between polaritons, mapping the system to the Lieb-Liniger model.
result: They demonstrate that the stationary light polaritons can realize the Lieb-Liniger model with tunable interaction strength, and analyze the resulting correlation functions and energy spectrum.
conclusion: This work provides a new platform for quantum simulation of interacting bosonic systems using hybrid light-matter excitations, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Metrology Based On Superconducting Qubits
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper explores quantum metrology using superconducting qubits, focusing on parameter estimation and sensitivity limits.
motivation: Quantum metrology with superconducting qubits can achieve high precision beyond classical limits, relevant for quantum sensing and computing.
method: The authors analyze the use of superconducting qubits as probes in quantum metrology protocols, likely employing Ramsey interferometry or similar techniques.
result: The paper demonstrates enhanced measurement sensitivity and discusses practical implementations with current superconducting qubit technology.
conclusion: Superconducting qubits are a promising platform for quantum metrology, with potential applications in sensing and fundamental physics.

title: Fully Passive Received Quantum Access Network Based On Reference-frame-independent Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 June 2026;
tldr: A fully passive received quantum access network based on reference-frame-independent QKD is proposed and demonstrated.
motivation: To reduce the complexity and cost of quantum access networks by eliminating active components at the receiver side, while maintaining security against reference frame misalignment.
method: The authors design a passive receiver architecture that uses a reference-frame-independent QKD protocol, and analyze its security and performance.
result: The proposed scheme achieves secure key rates comparable to active receiver designs, with improved practicality for network deployment.
conclusion: Fully passive received quantum access networks are feasible and can simplify quantum network infrastructure without compromising security.

title: Integrated High-quality Multi-wavelength Quantum Light Source Compatible With Itu Channel Grid
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates an integrated multi-wavelength quantum light source compatible with the ITU channel grid, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require multi-wavelength quantum light sources that are compatible with existing telecommunication infrastructure to enable efficient wavelength-division multiplexing.
method: The authors fabricate an integrated photonic chip using periodically poled lithium niobate waveguides to generate photon pairs via spontaneous parametric down-conversion at multiple ITU-grid wavelengths.
result: The source produces high-quality photon pairs with high brightness, low noise, and narrow bandwidths aligned to the ITU channel grid, suitable for quantum key distribution and other quantum network protocols.
conclusion: This integrated multi-wavelength source is a practical step toward scalable, wavelength-multiplexed quantum networks compatible with classical telecom systems.

title: Constant Runtime Error Mitigation Via Restricted Evolution
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: Proposes a constant-time error mitigation technique for quantum circuits by restricting the evolution to a subspace that is resilient to certain errors.
motivation: Error mitigation is crucial for near-term quantum devices, but existing methods often require many circuit repetitions or post-processing overhead. The authors aim to reduce runtime overhead.
method: The method restricts the quantum evolution to a subspace where errors are suppressed or correctable, using a combination of dynamical decoupling and symmetry constraints.
result: Demonstrates constant-time error mitigation on several benchmark circuits, showing improved fidelity compared to standard error mitigation techniques with lower overhead.
conclusion: The restricted evolution approach offers a practical, low-overhead error mitigation strategy suitable for near-term quantum processors.

title: Distributed Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm On A Quantum-centric Supercomputing Architecture
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a distributed implementation of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) on a quantum-centric supercomputing architecture, focusing on scalability and resource efficiency.
motivation: QAOA is a promising near-term quantum algorithm, but its practical application is limited by the size and quality of current quantum hardware. Distributing QAOA across multiple quantum processors could overcome these limitations.
method: The authors propose a distributed QAOA framework that partitions the problem graph into subgraphs, each solved by a separate quantum processor, with classical communication to coordinate updates. They demonstrate the approach on a simulated quantum-centric supercomputer.
result: The distributed QAOA achieves comparable approximation ratios to the monolithic version while reducing the required qubit count per processor, enabling larger problem instances. The overhead from classical communication is manageable for moderate problem sizes.
conclusion: Distributed QAOA is a viable path toward scaling quantum optimization algorithms, leveraging existing quantum hardware and classical supercomputing resources.

title: Superconductivity On Two Surfaces
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: Superconductivity observed in rhombohedral multilayer graphene with electrons and holes on opposite surfaces.
motivation: To explore unconventional superconductivity in a two-surface system within graphene.
method: Experimental study of rhombohedral multilayer graphene, measuring transport properties.
result: Superconductivity emerges from an unusual normal state with electrons and holes on opposite surfaces.
conclusion: The two-surface geometry provides a new platform for studying superconductivity.

title: Superconductivity From Dual-surface Carriers In Rhombohedral Graphene
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene arising from dual-surface carriers.
motivation: To explore unconventional superconductivity in graphene systems with multiple layers.
method: Experimental transport measurements on medium-thickness rhombohedral graphene devices.
result: Multiple superconducting states are observed, attributed to wavefunctions localized on the outer layers.
conclusion: Rhombohedral graphene hosts superconductivity from dual-surface carriers, offering a new platform for studying correlated phases.

title: Decoupling Adhesion From Jamming In Phase Transitions Drives Tissue Organization
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how adhesion and jamming phase transitions drive tissue organization in cellular collectives.
motivation: Understanding how physical parameters like cell density and adhesion control tissue material state and developmental programs.
method: Combines in silico modeling and in vivo experiments to independently tune cell density and adhesion.
result: Adhesion dictates the tissue material state; adhesion-driven solidification in unjammed pluripotent tissues drives epithelial organization.
conclusion: Phase transitions direct developmental programmes in tissues.

title: Suppression Of Coherent Light Scattering In A Three-dimensional Atomic Array
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: Experiments with a three-dimensional atomic array demonstrate strong omnidirectional suppression of coherent light scattering.
motivation: Previous studies of collective light scattering in atomic arrays focused on 1D and 2D systems; extending to 3D is important for understanding many-body light-matter interactions.
method: The authors experimentally realize a 3D atomic array and measure the suppression of coherent scattering in all directions.
result: They observe strong omnidirectional suppression of coherent light scattering, indicating collective subradiant behavior.
conclusion: 3D atomic arrays can exhibit collective optical effects not present in lower dimensions, with potential applications in quantum optics and information.

title: Watching Ionization In A New Light
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: MeV electron pulses induce strong modulation in optical transmission of semiconductors, enabling room-temperature detection of ionizing radiation with sub-10-ps timing precision.
motivation: To develop next-generation medical imaging and radiation diagnostics with high temporal resolution.
method: Experimental demonstration using MeV electron pulses and optical transmission measurement in common semiconductors.
result: Observation of surprisingly strong modulation enabling sub-10-ps timing precision at room temperature.
conclusion: The findings could lead to improved medical imaging and radiation diagnostics.

title: Is Ball Lightning A Relativistic Soliton?
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes that ball lightning is a relativistic soliton, supported by laser experiments producing millimeter-scale solitons.
motivation: Ball lightning is a poorly understood atmospheric phenomenon; the paper aims to explain it via relativistic solitons.
method: High-power laser experiments generate relativistic solitons in plasma, and their properties are compared to ball lightning observations.
result: Millimeter-scale relativistic solitons are produced, consistent with ball lightning characteristics.
conclusion: Relativistic solitons could be a viable explanation for ball lightning.

title: The Thin Line For Optical Neural Networks Towards Broad Practical Relevance
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper discusses the practical challenges and research priorities for optical neural networks, focusing on their real-world applicability rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Optical neural networks promise high efficiency and bandwidth, but their practical value for general-purpose or specialized applications needs validation under realistic conditions.
method: The paper reviews recent insights and outlines key research priorities for optical neural networks, likely through analysis of existing literature and identification of gaps.
result: The paper identifies critical challenges such as scalability, noise tolerance, and integration with electronic systems that must be addressed for broad practical relevance.
conclusion: Optical neural networks require further development to meet application-realistic benchmarks before they can achieve broad practical relevance.

title: High-speed Non-volatile Barium Titanate Field-programmable Photonic Gate Array
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: A high-speed non-volatile photonic programmable gate array using barium titanate ferroelectric phase shifters.
motivation: To achieve energy-efficient programmable photonic circuits with fast switching and non-volatile state retention.
method: Barium titanate ferroelectric material is used in photonic phase shifters arranged in a hexagonal waveguide mesh.
result: The device achieves sub-100-ns switching speeds and retains state without continuous power.
conclusion: This technology enables energy-efficient, high-speed programmable photonic integrated circuits.

title: Chaotic Photonics In Microresonators
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 May 2026;
tldr: A review of chaotic dynamics in microresonator photonics, covering various materials and architectures.
motivation: To survey how chaos in microcavities can be harnessed for photonic technologies and fundamental science.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical work on chaotic microcavities, including ray and wave chaos, mode coupling, and nonlinear effects.
result: Chaotic photonics enables novel functionalities such as broadband light generation, sensing, and random lasing.
conclusion: Harnessing chaos in microresonators offers new opportunities for photonic devices and fundamental studies.

title: Cross-probing Van Der Waals Multiferroics
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 15 May 2026;
tldr: A review advocating cross-probing techniques to identify intrinsic multiferroicity in van der Waals materials.
motivation: Van der Waals multiferroics offer potential for low-power magnetoelectric devices, but conventional probing methods struggle to distinguish intrinsic from extrinsic effects in atomically thin materials.
method: The review surveys cross-probing technologies that combine multiple characterization techniques (e.g., optical, electrical, magnetic) to probe coupled orders in 2D multiferroics.
result: Cross-probing methods can reliably identify intrinsic magnetoelectric coupling in van der Waals multiferroics, overcoming limitations of single-probe techniques.
conclusion: Cross-probing is essential for advancing the study and application of 2D multiferroics in low-power devices.

title: Vortices And Solitons In Polariton Superfluids And Condensates
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 14 May 2026;
tldr: A review of vortices and solitons in polariton superfluids and condensates, focusing on their formation and control for information processing.
motivation: Polariton systems exhibit nonlinear phenomena like vortices and solitons that could be harnessed for information processing, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review summarizes experimental and theoretical work on polariton condensates, discussing optical driving and nonlinear dynamics.
result: Vortices and solitons in polariton superfluids have quantized phase jumps and stable shapes, enabling potential applications.
conclusion: Polariton vortices and solitons are promising for information processing, but the paper lacks depth in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Superballistic Flow Of Viscous Electron Fluid Induced By Edge Magnetoplasmons In Point Contacts
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports superballistic electron flow in point contacts under microwave irradiation, attributed to edge magnetoplasmons.
motivation: To investigate hydrodynamic electron transport and superballistic flow in a viscous electron fluid.
method: Experimental measurement of electron transport through point contacts in a two-dimensional electron gas under microwave irradiation.
result: Observation of superballistic flow induced by edge magnetoplasmons.
conclusion: Edge magnetoplasmons can enhance electron flow beyond ballistic limits in viscous electron fluids.

title: Soft-X-ray Momentum Microscopy Of Nonlinear Magnon Interactions
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a soft-X-ray momentum microscopy technique to image nonlinear magnon interactions with nanoscale sensitivity.
motivation: Nonlinear magnon interactions are difficult to detect, limiting the study of nanoscale spin dynamics.
method: The authors use soft X-rays to image magnon momentum, enabling detection of nonlinear interactions.
result: The method captures nonlinear magnon interactions with nanometre-scale sensitivity.
conclusion: Soft-X-ray momentum microscopy is a powerful tool for studying magnon dynamics at the nanoscale.

title: Scaling Matters Of Cell Fate
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports a universal scaling law in DNA methylation dynamics during early embryo development, linking physical constraints to cell fate determination.
motivation: Understanding how cell differentiation is regulated is a fundamental question in developmental biology; the authors aim to uncover whether physical principles govern methylation dynamics.
method: The study analyzes methylation data from early embryos and identifies a scaling law that describes the dynamics across different species and conditions.
result: Methylation dynamics follow a universal scaling law, suggesting that physical constraints, rather than molecular specifics, shape cell fate.
conclusion: The findings imply that cell fate determination is governed by universal physical principles, which could have implications for regenerative medicine and developmental biology.

title: Evidence For The Generic Existence Of Two Local Structures In Liquid Water
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: Simulations suggest the existence of two interconvertible local structures in liquid water, supporting the two-state model of deeply undercooled water.
motivation: Understanding the structure of liquid water, especially under deeply undercooled conditions, is important for condensed matter physics and chemistry.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations were performed to analyze local structural motifs in liquid water.
result: Evidence for two distinct local structures that undergo interconvertible reactions was found, corroborating the two-state picture.
conclusion: The two-state model of water is supported by simulation evidence, providing insight into water's anomalous properties.

title: Metasurfaces Bridge The Terahertz Gap
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: A nonlinear metasurface enables widely tunable continuous-wave terahertz emission at room temperature, bridging the terahertz gap.
motivation: The terahertz spectral region is difficult to access with compact, room-temperature sources; a practical solution is needed for applications in imaging, spectroscopy, and communications.
method: The authors engineer a nonlinear metasurface with a carefully designed structure to achieve efficient, tunable continuous-wave terahertz generation via nonlinear optical processes.
result: The metasurface produces widely tunable terahertz radiation at room temperature, offering a compact and efficient source.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to compact terahertz sources, potentially enabling new applications in the terahertz range.

title: Time-varying Photonics Enables Polarization Control
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates dynamic polarization control using time-varying photonics in an epsilon-near-zero material.
motivation: To achieve ultrafast polarization control for photonic applications.
method: Optical pumping of an isotropic aluminium zinc oxide film near its epsilon-near-zero regime induces birefringence, dichroism, and optical activity.
result: Sub-picosecond timescale polarization control is demonstrated.
conclusion: Time-varying photonics in epsilon-near-zero materials enables dynamic polarization manipulation.

title: Atomic Force Microscopy From Nanoscale Imaging To Holistic Exploration
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: A commentary on the evolution of atomic force microscopy from imaging to a versatile nanoscience platform.
motivation: To highlight the broad impact and versatility of atomic force microscopy beyond its original imaging purpose.
method: Historical review and commentary on key innovations in AFM technology.
result: AFM has become a multifunctional tool for nanoscale characterization, manipulation, and measurement.
conclusion: AFM continues to expand its role in nanoscience, enabling new experiments and applications.

title: Do The Benefits Of Fundamental Physics Research Outweigh Its Wider Societal Costs?
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 27 May 2026;
tldr: This paper discusses the societal costs and benefits of fundamental physics research using economic tools, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To evaluate whether large-scale fundamental physics projects are sustainable and beneficial to society.
method: Applies economic decision-making tools to assess the multi-dimensional problem of big science sustainability.
result: The paper argues that economic tools can help evaluate the trade-offs of fundamental physics research.
conclusion: Decision-making for big science projects should incorporate economic analysis to weigh societal costs and benefits.

title: Automated Synthesis Of InSb Quantum Dots With Improved Batch-to-batch Reproducibility Via Kinetically Matched Co-reduction
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents an automated synthesis method for InSb colloidal quantum dots using kinetically matched co-reduction to improve batch-to-batch reproducibility and size uniformity.
motivation: InSb quantum dots are promising heavy metal-free infrared materials, but manual synthesis leads to poor reproducibility and size control, hindering practical applications.
method: The authors developed an automated platform that uses kinetically matched co-reduction of indium and antimony precursors, with real-time monitoring and feedback control to achieve consistent reaction conditions.
result: The automated synthesis produced InSb quantum dots with significantly improved batch-to-batch reproducibility and narrower size distribution compared to manual synthesis.
conclusion: Automated, kinetically controlled synthesis enables scalable production of high-quality InSb quantum dots, advancing their use in infrared optoelectronics.

title: Adhesion-driven Rigidity Transition Decoupled From Density-driven Jamming Triggers Epithelial Organization In Embryonic Tissues
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 02 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies adhesion-driven rigidity transitions in embryonic tissues, unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding how epithelial tissues organize during morphogenesis is a key question in developmental biology.
method: The authors use experimental and theoretical approaches to decouple adhesion-driven rigidification from density-driven jamming in embryonic tissues.
result: They identify that adhesion-driven rigidification is a key trigger for epithelial organization, but only when uncoupled from density-driven jamming.
conclusion: Adhesion-driven rigidity transitions play a crucial role in tissue organization during embryonic development.

title: Implosion Carving Shrinks 3D-printed Nanostructures
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: A nanofabrication technique using hydrogel swelling and controlled shrinkage to create high-refractive-index-contrast 3D nanostructures for visible-light photonics.
motivation: To enable fabrication of nanometre-scale 3D photonic structures with high refractive index contrast for visible-light applications, which is challenging with conventional methods.
method: The method involves 3D printing a swollen hydrogel structure, then controlled shrinkage (implosion carving) to reduce feature sizes and increase refractive index contrast.
result: The technique produces high-refractive-index-contrast, nanometre-scale 3D photonic structures suitable for visible-light applications.
conclusion: Implosion carving is a promising approach for fabricating complex 3D nanostructures for photonics, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Exploring Decolonizing The Curriculum Using Six Thinking Hats
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: The paper discusses decolonizing the physics curriculum using the Six Thinking Hats framework to facilitate structured conversations.
motivation: Decolonizing physics curricula is a scientific necessity but often stalled by competence anxiety among educators.
method: The authors propose using Edward de Bono's Six Thinking Hats framework to structure and safely navigate challenging conversations about decolonization.
result: The framework provides a structured approach to address decolonization, potentially reducing anxiety and enabling progress.
conclusion: The Six Thinking Hats method can help educators engage in decolonizing curricula in a constructive and safe manner.

title: Transparent Conducting Electrodes For Perovskite–silicon Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 27 May 2026;
tldr: A review of transparent conducting electrodes for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells, focusing on optical, electrical, and interfacial losses.
motivation: Transparent conducting electrodes are a key performance and sustainability bottleneck in high-efficiency tandem solar cells.
method: The review examines how losses arise and outlines strategies for scalable, low-indium electrodes.
result: Identifies strategies to reduce indium usage and improve electrode performance.
conclusion: Scalable, low-indium electrodes are critical for next-generation tandem solar cells.

title: Transitions Of The Atlantic Ocean Circulation
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 18 May 2026;
tldr: This paper reviews the multistable dynamics of the Atlantic Ocean circulation from a dynamical systems perspective, focusing on climate physics.
motivation: Understanding instabilities in the Atlantic Ocean circulation is crucial for predicting large climate impacts.
method: The authors unify results from a hierarchy of ocean-climate models using a dynamical systems viewpoint.
result: The review synthesizes knowledge on transitions and multistability of the Atlantic circulation.
conclusion: The dynamical systems approach provides a coherent framework for studying ocean circulation instabilities and their climate implications.

title: Genomic And Ecological Drivers Of Parallel Arid Adaptation In Tree Grapes (Vitaceae)
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the genomic basis of succulence evolution in tree grapes, focusing on long terminal repeat retrotransposons.
motivation: Succulence is a key drought-resistance trait, but its genomic basis is underexplored.
method: Comparative genomics and phylogenetic analyses of Vitaceae species.
result: Long terminal repeat retrotransposons inserted into introns may facilitate succulence evolution and genomic adaptability.
conclusion: The study provides insights into parallel arid adaptation in tree grapes.

title: Intermolecular Interactions Optimization In Weakly Solvating Ether Solvents For Wide-temperature Na Metal Batteries
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper optimizes intermolecular interactions in weakly solvating ether solvents to enable wide-temperature Na metal batteries.
motivation: To extend the operating temperature range of Na metal batteries for broader applications.
method: Developed high-boiling-point, weakly solvating electrolytes and analyzed intermolecular interactions.
result: Achieved Na metal batteries operable from -40 to 70 °C.
conclusion: Intermolecular interactions in electrolytes are key to wide-temperature reversibility.

title: Tmem63b Regulates Nucleocytoplasmic Transport And Placental Development
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the role of Tmem63b in nucleocytoplasmic transport and placental development, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying placental development is important for reproductive biology and developmental disorders.
method: The authors likely used genetic knockout models, cell biology assays, and imaging to investigate Tmem63b function.
result: Tmem63b regulates nucleocytoplasmic transport and is essential for proper placental development.
conclusion: Tmem63b is a key regulator of placental development through its role in nucleocytoplasmic transport.

title: Grain Boundary Engineered Aluminum Current Collector For Energy-dense Initially Anode-free Sodium Metal Batteries
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a grain boundary engineered aluminum current collector for anode-free sodium metal batteries, focusing on energy density and battery performance.
motivation: To improve the energy density and safety of sodium metal batteries by designing a current collector that compensates for sodium loss and stabilizes plating/stripping.
method: A Ga-rich polycrystalline aluminum current collector is engineered with controlled grain boundaries to enable Al3+ dissolution and regulate sodium deposition.
result: The engineered current collector enables reversible sodium plating/stripping and delivers high-performance anode-free sodium metal batteries.
conclusion: Grain boundary engineering of current collectors is a promising strategy for advancing energy-dense sodium metal batteries.

title: Cryo-EM Structures Of Heteromeric Kir4.1/5.1 Channel Suggest Mechanisms Of Inward Rectification And Channel Blockage
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: Cryo-EM structures of Kir4.1/5.1 channels reveal mechanisms of inward rectification and polyamine blockage.
motivation: Understanding the structural basis of inward rectification and channel blockage in Kir4.1/5.1 channels, which are important for brain and kidney function.
method: Combined cryo-electron microscopy, electrophysiology, and computational studies to determine channel structures and blockage mechanisms.
result: Identified an inner-ring pore blockage mechanism by polyamines and inhibitors, providing structural insights into inward rectification.
conclusion: The study elucidates the structural basis for inward rectification and channel blockage, which may inform therapeutic targeting.

title: Towards Practical Aqueous Zinc Metal Pouch Cell Batteries Via Weakly Bound Water-mediated Shear-thickening Electrolyte
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a shear-thickening electrolyte for aqueous zinc metal pouch cell batteries to suppress dendrites and corrosion.
motivation: Dendrite growth and corrosion limit the performance of zinc metal electrodes in aqueous batteries, so a new electrolyte design is needed.
method: The authors design a weakly bound water-mediated shear-thickening electrolyte that combines chemical regulation with mechanical reinforcement.
result: The electrolyte effectively suppresses dendrites and corrosion, enabling stable zinc metal electrodes.
conclusion: The proposed electrolyte offers a practical approach to improving aqueous zinc metal pouch cell batteries.
